question: In carbamate poisoning, pralidoxime is equally essential as in organophosphate poisoning because both cause irreversible inhibition of acetylcholinesterase.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Organophosphates cause irreversible phosphorylation of AChE (which undergoes 'ageing'), requiring pralidoxime to reactivate the enzyme before ageing occurs. Carbamates cause reversible carbamylation — enzyme activity recovers spontaneously in hours, so pralidoxime is not needed.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Carbamate inhibition of AChE is spontaneously reversible (carbamylation is unstable; enzyme activity recovers within hours without oxime treatment). Pralidoxime is generally not required and may be ineffective. Atropine alone is the mainstay. In contrast, organophosphate inhibition is irreversible and undergoes 'ageing', making early pralidoxime essential.
